messages:
morgan: heads up - after the global rebalancer sweep at 02:05 UTC we're seeing a cluster of nvme remap events in us-central1 scratch nodes. GPU attach latencies crept up.
infra-bot: Alert NVME_REMAP_RATE high on us-central1 (hosts: gnode-421, gnode-422, gnode-430). Triggered at 02:12 UTC.
morgan: quick dmesg excerpt from gnode-421:
```
[02:11:58] nvme0: async remap queued, remap_count=14
[02:12:02] nvme0: iops_drop, qdepth=2048, attach_wait=900ms
[02:12:10] nvme0: crc_warn=1, remap_rate=120/s
```
ravi: that qdepth is scary. did rebalancer flood tempfiles onto hotstripe?
sara: looks like rebalancer created many small files during move, janitor kicked in at same time. concurrency for janitor was default 10.
irene: i've throttled the rebalancer to 15 nodes/min and set janitor concurrency to 3 for us-central1: `infractl rebalancer set-rate --zone us-central1 --rate 15` and `infractl janitor set-concurrency --zone us-central1 3`.
morgan: thanks. any idea if firmware plays here? ops-bot: SMART report (gnode-421 nvme0): `FW_VER=4.0.0, Reallocated=0, Media_Err=0, Temp=36C`
ravi: fw looks recent. maybe controller buffer exhaustion when many tiny writes + garbage collection.
sara: temporary workaround: reroute nonlatency-sensitive GPU attaches to dedicated pool in us-east1 and mark suspect nodes readonly for scheduling.
irene: marking gnode-421/422 readonly and draining new attaches.
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-467 opened (nvme remap surge - us-central1). Pager: oncall-storage.
morgan: can we reduce per-device write concurrency at kernel level until we have a full postmortem? i can push `echo 256 > /sys/block/nvme0/queue/nr_requests` to cap queue depth.
ravi: do that on the fenced nodes only. lowering nr_requests to 256 reduced immediate tail latency on a test node.
sara: metrics show remap_rate fell from ~120/s -> ~30/s in 6 minutes after throttles. attach p95 latency back to baseline-ish.
irene: scheduling a maintenance window to replace 2 drives that show elevated remap counters even though SMART is nominal. replacement during low-traffic window tomorrow 03:00-05:00 UTC.
ops-bot: FYI shifting jobs adds ~9% cost delta for the hour. approved by ops.
morgan: action items: 1) keep rebalancer rate low for 24h (irene) 2) lower janitor concurrency zone-wide (irene) 3) fence/read-only suspect hosts (irene/morgan) 4) schedule drive replacements (irene) 5) RFC for rebalancer/janitor backpressure integration with storage metrics (ravi).
ravi: i'll draft RFC `rfc/storage-rebalancer-handshake` and include threshold suggestions: remap_rate>50/s or device_qdepth>1500 -> slow ramp.
sara: note for postmortem - include correlation between small-write churn (files/sec) and nvme remap_rate; also test 4.1.0-rc fw on a canary host.
morgan: thanks all. moving discussion & logs to INC-2026-467. ping me if remap_rate resurges. :thumbsup:
